clue.text: Set of green stones: possibly fifty remade on punishment in South Africa

indicators.note: 'possibly' says the letters that follow could be one of several arrangements, so they are shuffled

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
taken as written; its own meaning also hints at rebuilding
necklacing was a mob killing with a burning tyre placed round the victim's neck, used in apartheid-era South African townships

explanation.surface: A string of green gems is described alongside a grim note about a punishment once used in South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means placed above, so the shuffled gem word sits on top of the punishment word.
explanation.definitionFit: A necklace of emerald gemstones is literally a strung set of green precious stones worn round the throat.

clue.text: Stations open all day for this national event

definitions.text: Stations open all day for this national event

parts.note: surface reading: railway or radio stations running round the clock
setter's reading: polling stations stay open all day while the whole country votes

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stations' suggests trains or broadcasting; the stations meant are polling stations, where voters cast their ballots.
explanation.definitionFit: On a nationwide voting day, polling stations stay open from morning to night so every citizen can choose a parliament.

clue.text: Venue for fire drill?

parts.note: surface reading: practising evacuation when the alarm rings
setter's reading: a place where people practise firing guns

explanation.walkthrough: A fire drill is normally an evacuation rehearsal; read as 'firing practice' it points to where marksmen train.
explanation.definitionFit: Shooters practise firing weapons at targets in a dedicated area, which is where their shooting drill takes place.

clue.text: Cover prior to shelling

parts.note: surface reading: taking cover before an artillery bombardment
setter's reading: removing the shell from a boiled egg at breakfast

explanation.walkthrough: 'Shelling' sounds military, but here it means peeling a boiled egg; the cover keeps it warm until then.
explanation.definitionFit: A small padded hood keeps a boiled egg warm at the table until someone cracks and peels it.

clue.text: Eastern hideaway is paradise

parts.note: E is the standard abbreviation for east or eastern
a den is a secluded retreat or lair

explanation.surface: A secluded retreat somewhere in the East is described as heavenly.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical garden where Adam and Eve lived is the archetype of a perfect, blissful place.

clue.text: Pork — in slices!

parts.note: surface reading: a cut of pig meat, sliced up
setter's reading: cured pig meat placed between slices of bread

explanation.walkthrough: 'In slices' looks like 'sliced', but means 'inside slices of bread'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rashers of cured pig meat served between two pieces of bread make a classic British snack.

clue.text: On his off days he's matchless!

definitions.text: On his off days he's matchless!

parts.words: On his off days he's matchless!
parts.note: surface reading: someone who is unbeatable even when not on form
setter's reading: on days when he is off duty this official has no game to take charge of

explanation.walkthrough: 'Matchless' usually means peerless; here it means literally without a match to officiate.
explanation.definitionFit: The official who runs a soccer game has no fixture to control on days when he is not working.

clue.text: In pain, limped in garage, hindering progress

indicators.note: 'In' says the solution is found inside the words that follow, rather than built from them

parts.note: the letters run on from inside the first word through to the start of the last

explanation.surface: Someone hobbles painfully into a car workshop, struggling to get anywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts after the L of limped and ends at the G of garage.
explanation.definitionFit: Obstructing someone or something is getting in the way of its advance, which is what holding up movement means.

clue.text: Fierce person has no backing after dreary business

parts.note: a drag is a tedious, boring affair

indicators.note: 'backing' means going backwards, so the short word is read from its end

parts.note: taken as written, before it is turned round

explanation.surface: Someone formidable refuses to offer support after some tiresome dealings.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragon is informally a fearsome, domineering person, often a stern older woman.

clue.text: Confused, Dora partly absorbs the French test

indicators.note: something confused is muddled up, so the letters of the name are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
le is the masculine French word for 'the'

explanation.surface: A muddled girl called Dora half takes in a French exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Partly absorbs' describes the result: the jumbled name takes the E inside while the L stays outside at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordeal is a severe trial, and historically a trial by ordeal was a physical test of guilt.

clue.text: Associates with criminal types

parts.note: a con is a convict, short for convicted criminal
sorts are kinds or types

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one phrase, but it splits into the definition and two pieces for crooks and kinds.
explanation.definitionFit: To consort with people is to keep company or habitually spend time alongside them.

clue.text: Appeal of jump leads

indicators.note: 'of' here means 'taken out of', so the solution is drawn from inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters straddle the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: It reads like a request involving jump leads, the cables used to start a car with a flat battery.
explanation.definitionFit: A plea is an earnest request or entreaty, which is what an appeal is.

clue.text: Talented beginner certain to shine?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a newcomer quickly becoming successful
second meaning, playful: a star climbing in the sky is bound to shine

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the second meaning is literal astronomy rather than a description of a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A promising newcomer heading for fame is called this, while a celestial body coming up over the horizon will glitter.

clue.text: They act impulsively out of anxiety about locked room

indicators.note: 'about' means surrounding, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: nerves are feelings of anxiety
a cell is a room where a prisoner is locked in

explanation.surface: People behave rashly because they are anxious about being shut in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Impulsively' is the joke: these cells work by electrical impulses.
explanation.definitionFit: Neurons carry information around the body by transmitting electrical impulses, so they literally operate by impulse.

clue.text: Girl turned on insect — insect bit

parts.note: an ant is an insect; the second 'insect' in the clue belongs to the definition

indicators.note: 'turned' means turned round, so the name is read from back to front

parts.note: Anne is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl rounds on a bug, and the bug bites her.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' means placed after, so the turned name follows the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: An antenna is one of the feelers on an insect's head, so it is a part of the creature.

clue.text: Fold right inside mollusc

indicators.note: 'inside' places one piece within the other

parts.note: a winkle is a small edible sea snail
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A crease sits snugly within a shellfish.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrinkle is a small crease or ridge in skin or fabric, the same as a small fold.

clue.text: Standards set by including Queen in wedding announcement

indicators.note: 'including' means taking in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: banns are the church notice of an intended marriage
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: Rules of etiquette are fixed by putting the monarch into a marriage notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standards' suggests norms of behaviour; here they are flags.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a flag carried on a pole, and a banner is likewise a flag or ensign.

clue.text: Create lace model and so speed up

indicators.note: to model is to shape or fashion, so the letters are moulded into a new form

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone makes and models lace quickly to work faster.
explanation.definitionFit: To accelerate is to increase velocity, the same as going faster.

clue.text: Mixing with sailors, we get the bird

indicators.note: 'Mixing' means stirring the letters together into a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written
RN is the Royal Navy, whose members are sailors

explanation.surface: Socialising with the navy, we end up being rejected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get the bird' is an idiom for being booed or dismissed; here it is just the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The wren is a tiny brown songbird common in British gardens.

clue.text: Dull club produces pressing item

parts.note: flat means lifeless or dull
an iron is a type of golf club

explanation.surface: A boring golf club turns out to be a useful household tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pressing' suggests urgent; it means ironing clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A flatiron is an old-fashioned iron heated on a stove and used to smooth laundry.

clue.text: Sounds like the route travelled by bicycle

indicators.note: 'Sounds like' asks for a word pronounced the same as the next word but spelt differently

parts.note: a road is a route; the past tense of ride is pronounced identically

explanation.surface: It describes the path someone followed on a bike ride.
explanation.definitionFit: Riding is how one travels on a bike, and the past tense of ride describes a completed journey.

clue.text: Formed a strong impression from sketch editor made

indicators.note: 'from' says the solution is taken out of the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run from inside the first word into the start of the second

explanation.surface: An editor's drawing left a lasting mark on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Etching cuts lines deep into a surface, so it figuratively means leaving a permanent, vivid impression.

clue.text: Agreement reached by putting material on account

indicators.note: in an across clue 'on' means attached after, so the first-named thing goes behind the second

parts.note: AC is the usual abbreviation for account
cord is a ribbed fabric, short for corduroy

explanation.surface: A deal is struck by charging some fabric to a customer's account.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' means placed after, so the material follows the account abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: An accord is a formal treaty or settlement, which is a kind of agreement between parties.

clue.text: Being released, deer live freely

definitions.note: a participial phrase; the answer is the matching past participle, as in 'relieved of duty'

indicators.note: 'freely' means without fixed form, so the letters roam into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Freed from captivity, deer roam at liberty.
explanation.definitionFit: To be relieved of a duty or burden is to be freed from it, as a sentry is when the guard changes.
